citations.name: requirements.sdk.domain
citations.commentary:
An *application domain* is the application's graph, node contents, and evidence
storage, made available together for criterion execution. In the SDK, it
implements [`Domain`](../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/domain/trait.Domain.html) to supply
its shared types, node and edge operations, and evidence persistence.

rationale: The commentary at `md/requirements/sdk.md` (the block inside the "Defining the application domain" section) is explanatory prose, so `{cite}` is the right role. Its claims agree with `requirements.sdk.domain`. The requirement says every application domain implements `trust_but_verify::domain::Domain`. The trait's associated types (`Error`, `NodeId`, `NodeContent`, `EdgeLabel`) are the "shared types". The methods `node_path`, `node_content` and `outgoing_edges` are the "node and edge operations". The methods `load_evidence` and `store_evidence` are "evidence persistence". The passage's definition of the term, bundling the graph, node contents and evidence storage for criterion execution, is a reasonable gloss of the trait and does not contradict the requirement. No claim is contradicted or unsupported, and the passage has no redundant `{impl}` or `{test}` citation of the same requirement.
